clue.text: Go to visit fox? Abandon this fantasy!

parts.note: to go and visit someone, dropping in on them
an earth is the burrow where a fox lives, so the fox stands for its home

explanation.surface: Someone dreaming of paying a call on a fox is told to snap out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: COME DOWN TO EARTH: a fox's den is called its earth, so visiting the fox means going down to its earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to reality after daydreaming, which is exactly giving up a fantasy.

clue.text: Chose more tomato salad that had nasty consequences for one

definitions.text: that had nasty consequences for one

indicators.note: a salad is a tossed mixture, so the preceding words are tossed into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who picked a bigger tomato salad suffered for it afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: CAME HOME TO ROOST, like chickens returning at dusk, describes past misdeeds catching up with the person responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said of bad actions whose unpleasant effects eventually fall back on whoever committed them.

clue.text: Staff alternative country house

parts.note: to staff something is to man it
the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A choice of personnel for a stately home in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as a noun but works as the verb meaning to provide workers for.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is the principal residence on a rural estate, historically the lord's dwelling.

clue.text: Flat due for renovation but a failure to do it

indicators.note: a renovation reworks a property, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An apartment is scheduled for a makeover, but the work never gets done.
explanation.definitionFit: Default is the neglect of an obligation, such as not paying a debt or not appearing when required.

clue.text: A film of our civilisation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cowboy movie set in the American frontier
second meaning: belonging to the culture of Europe and America

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a documentary about our society; the two parts are separate senses of WESTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns are a cinema genre about cowboys, and Western also describes Occidental culture as opposed to Eastern.

clue.text: Actors on tour store up plays

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so these letters get moved around

parts.note: seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A touring theatre company keeps a stock of scripts to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Troupes are companies of performers, typically travelling from venue to venue to stage their shows.

clue.text: Stand before entrance barrier needing to be raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters lifts them so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before
a gate bars an entrance

explanation.surface: A stall placed in front of a gate that has to be lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are joined first and the whole string is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An etagere is a piece of furniture with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a type of display stand.

clue.text: Judge has purpose in period for public consultations

parts.note: a referee, who judges a game

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, held within the time span

parts.note: an era is a period of history
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A judge with a mission during a particular period.
explanation.walkthrough: The purpose sits inside the period, after the judge; REFERENDA is the Latin plural, used alongside referendums.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are votes in which the whole electorate is asked directly to decide a single question.

clue.text: School break in sum– ?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a pause in the school year
setter's reading: the word for the hot season stops halfway, so only half the term appears before the break

explanation.walkthrough: The truncated 'sum–' is the season's name with half its letters, a visual joke on the mid-term holiday that splits a school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-term holiday is the short week-long break in the middle of a British school term.

clue.text: Clear O for what hopes to attract many Xs

definitions.text: what hopes to attract many Xs

parts.note: manifest means plain or obvious
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty a circle, like a noughts-and-crosses game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Xs are not kisses or crosses in a game but marks on ballot papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published programme of policies is designed to win votes, which are marked with a cross.

clue.text: Legal to be executed? That's dreadful

indicators.note: execution by beheading removes the head, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: permitted by law

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is terrible for an execution to be lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and dreadful are synonyms, both meaning very bad or shocking.

clue.text: Woman's clothing said to be shaggy

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, and we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: a suit belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A lady's outfit is described as rough and hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means covered in hair, a learned synonym for shaggy or hairy.

clue.text: Seaside clown, and maybe why his theatre is closed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the white-faced entertainer of old seaside shows

definitions.text: maybe why his theatre is closed
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, decay in the jetty where the show is staged

explanation.walkthrough: Split as PIER ROT: British seaside resorts had theatres at the end of their piers, which could be shut if the timbers decayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot was the stock French pantomime character, adopted by troupes performing in British seaside resorts.

clue.text: Concerning, drinking unknown whiskey

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A worry about someone drinking a mystery whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is whiskey distilled from rye grain, a classic North American style.

clue.text: In Franglais, October is wet a little

parts.note: the French word for month, used in the mixed French-English jargon
October is the tenth month of the year

explanation.surface: A remark about how some French-English mixture renders the name of an autumn month.
explanation.walkthrough: In half-French, October is 'mois ten', month number ten; the Franglais gives the French half and the English number.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to make it slightly damp, wetting it a little.

clue.text: Easily provoked, slice a rib in pieces

indicators.note: broken into pieces, these letters can be reassembled differently

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A short-tempered butcher hacks a rib into bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Irascible describes someone quick to anger, with a short temper.

clue.text: The Origin of (some) Species

definitions.meaning: surface reading: the title of Darwin's book on evolution
setter's reading: what many creatures, birds and reptiles among them, start life from

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'some' turns Darwin's title into a literal description of where many animals begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds, reptiles, fish and insects hatch from eggs, so for those species an egg is where each life begins.

clue.text: More demanding guide to go round our ships

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to steer is to guide
the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A tougher pilot is needed to take a vessel around the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' signals British: RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict or severe, so its comparative describes something more exacting.

clue.text: Japanese fish: the answer is initially obvious

indicators.note: what is plain at the start of each word is its opening letter, so we keep the initials

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A setter teasingly insists the name of a Japanese fish should be plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is true: the solution is spelt by the first letters of the three words after the colon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai is the Japanese sea bream, a fish prized in Japan and served on celebratory occasions.

clue.text: Pop these in a pot and rudely eat lots

indicators.note: doing something rudely means roughly, so this word is roughly rearranged

parts.note: three letters to be rearranged
bags of something means plenty of it

explanation.surface: Throw them in the pot and tuck in greedily, like a hungry guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea bags are small porous sachets of leaves dropped into a teapot to brew.

clue.text: Are a month old? This is a century old

parts.note: art is the old second-person form, as in 'thou art'
the abbreviation for December
a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is only weeks old, answered by something a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: ART DECO is the design style of the 1920s and 30s, so about a century has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative style flourished roughly a hundred years ago, so it is now about a century old.

clue.text: Splash drops over small pitch

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for small
a salesman's pitch is his patter

explanation.surface: Raindrops landing on a little sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a playing field but means sales talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to scatter small drops of liquid over something, splashing it.

clue.text: Cleaning seat, start to cheer City

parts.note: the opening of the cheer 'hip, hip, hooray'
Bath is a city in the west of England

explanation.surface: A fan wipes down a stadium seat before cheering on City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a football club, but it is Bath, an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip bath is a small tub in which one sits to wash, immersed only to the hips.

clue.text: Two heights enclose a harbour of very little value once

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: an old word for a tiny amount worth almost nothing

indicators.note: to enclose is to surround, so the middle material is wrapped by the outer pair

parts.note: two lots of H, the abbreviation for height
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Two hills surround a harbour that was formerly worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: HA'PORTH is short for halfpennyworth; the halfpenny was an old British coin, so 'once' marks the dated term.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfpennyworth was the smallest purchase possible, and the word came to mean a trifling amount.

clue.text: Bishop quietly taking on brief quarrel

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
taken as written
a tiff is a short, petty row

explanation.surface: A cleric calmly engaging in a short squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiff is a title for a bishop, especially the Pope as Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Vegetable repeats in the stomach

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the body, so we look inside the word's belly

parts.note: the letters sitting in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A vegetable that keeps coming back up after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeats' is the surface's indigestion, but it is only the word that hides the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a small round green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Cheese is extravagant in one of the Costas

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: Costa Rica, the Central American country
over the top, i.e. excessive

explanation.surface: A cheese is said to be lavish at a Spanish beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Costas' suggests Spain's holiday coasts, but the one needed is Costa Rica.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, mild Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Do this on the donkey or duck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the party game in which a blindfolded child fixes a tail to a donkey picture
second meaning: a dabbling duck with a long pointed tail

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is the action of the children's game 'pin the tail on the donkey'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the party game's action, and it is also a slender duck named for its sharp tail feathers.

clue.text: Fail to wear a uniform and I'll see you

indicators.note: something worn is put on around the body, so the outer letters dress the inner one

parts.note: A plus U, uniform in the NATO alphabet
to die is to stop working, as an engine fails

explanation.surface: A recruit who won't put on the uniform is shown the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell, used in English like 'goodbye' or 'see you'.

clue.text: Spanish man's first to leave card game

indicators.note: the first letter departs, so the word starts one letter later

parts.note: the Spanish word for man

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is the first player to quit a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'man's' is 'is', linking the wordplay to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre was a popular trick-taking card game of the 17th and 18th centuries, originating in Spain.

clue.text: In panic, if retired, shaking

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trembles with alarm at the thought of retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrified describes being gripped by extreme fear, the state of someone panicking.

clue.text: A cryptic clue for the Y in 'Independence Day'

definitions.text: A cryptic clue for the Y
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the letter Y is the last of four letters in the name of the summer month, so this phrase clues it
surface reading: the American national holiday

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reverses the usual process: the answer is itself a cryptic clue for Y, which is the final character of the seventh month's name, and also the American holiday's date.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans celebrate their Declaration of Independence on that date in July every year, so it names the holiday.
